title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Third edition, Volume 12, MIE-NEG - EB.5
text: (a) Great part of the hill of Bineves in Locahaber is composed of a kind of porphyry. It is remarkably fine, beautiful, and of an elegant reddish color; 1⁄2 in which (days Mr Williams), the pale role, the bluh, and the yellowish white colours, are finely blended and faded, through the body of the flone; which is of a jelly- like texture, and is undoubtedly one of the finet and mole elegant those in the world. On this hill alo is found a kind of porphyry of a growth colony with a living of brownish red. It is smooth, compact, and heavy; of a clote uniform texture, but has no brightened when broken. It has angular fpecks in it of a white quartzy fuhlance<sup>?</sup>
